title: Live agent edit, unapproved discounts, and looping replies: 4-stage refactor

stages.scenario: A service team runs a customer-facing Agentforce agent. An administrator edited the live agent's instructions in production for a new promotion. Within hours the agent offered 40% discounts nobody approved and looped on order-tracking questions. What is the root cause?

options.text: Editing the live agent put the change before customers with no test run first
options.coachingFeedback: Versioning lets a change be built as a new version and batch-tested in a sandbox while the active version keeps serving customers, with rollback to the last good version. Skipping that gate let one edit introduce both failures at once.

options.text: The discount rule sits in agent instructions instead of an action that checks approved promotions
options.coachingFeedback: An action-level check would have blocked the discounts, but not the order-tracking loop. Both symptoms began with the same edit, so the failure to fix first is how that edit reached customers.

options.text: The new promotion instructions overlap the order-tracking topic, so tracking questions are misclassified and loop
options.coachingFeedback: Topic overlap could explain the looping tracking questions, but not the unapproved discounts. Both appeared with one edit, which points to the path that edit took into production.

stages.scenario: The team will rebuild the agent. Promotions change weekly, discounts above 10% need manager approval, and the order-tracking loop came from overlapping topic instructions. Which design should the architect use?

options.text: Keep a single topic, and route every discount the agent grants to a supervisor queue for review
options.coachingFeedback: Reviewing every discount holds up the small ones that need no approval, and a single topic keeps the overlapping instructions that caused the tracking loop.

options.text: Separate topics per intent, with the approval threshold written into each topic's instructions
options.coachingFeedback: Separate topics fix the overlap, but an approval rule in instructions is interpreted by the model and can be overridden by prompt injection or unusual phrasing, so a discount can still slip through.

options.text: Separate topics per intent, with discounts applied only by an action that enforces the approval threshold
options.coachingFeedback: An approval check inside an action runs as code outside the reasoning loop, so no phrasing can skip it, and discounts under 10% still flow without review. Distinct topics give tracking questions their own instructions, removing the overlap behind the loop.

stages.scenario: The rebuilt agent passes its batch tests in a Full Copy sandbox. The live agent handles about 20,000 conversations a week, and human agents take escalations through Omni-Channel. How should the team release the new version?

options.text: Activate the new version for all conversations on a low-traffic weekend, after a final batch test
options.coachingFeedback: Sandbox tests cannot cover the variety of real customer conversations, and a full switch exposes every customer to whatever they missed at once.

options.text: Release to a small share of conversations first, keeping the prior version ready for rollback
options.coachingFeedback: A canary release exposes the new version to real, varied conversations while few customers are affected, and versioning lets admins reactivate the last good version if metrics slip. Omni-Channel escalation stays in place for the exposed share.

options.text: Run the new version internally with service reps posing as customers for a month before launch
options.coachingFeedback: Role-play adds cases, but staff draw on what the team already expects customers to say, and launch day still exposes all 20,000 weekly conversations at once.

stages.scenario: After full rollout, the team must spot topic misclassification, failing actions, and rising escalation rates within a day, and trace any bad answer to the reasoning step that produced it. What should the team use?

options.text: Nightly Testing Center batch runs of the regression test set, alerting admins when scores drop
options.coachingFeedback: Scheduled test runs catch drift on known scenarios, but they cannot show what real customers are asking or trace a specific live answer back to its reasoning.

options.text: Agentforce Analytics and Utterance Analysis for trends, with Session Tracing for reasoning-level root cause
options.coachingFeedback: Analytics and Utterance Analysis report what users request and whether the agent handled it, across all conversations. The Session Tracing Data Model records each turn's reasoning, actions, and inputs and outputs under a session ID, which tracing a bad answer requires.

options.text: A weekly sample of 200 transcripts scored by team leads for accuracy and escalation quality
options.coachingFeedback: A weekly sample misses the one-day window, and a transcript shows what the agent said, not which topic, action, or reasoning step produced it.
